title: Distribution-Free, Risk-Controlling Prediction Sets
abstract: While improving prediction accuracy has been the focus of machine learning in recent years, this alone does not suffice for reliable decision-making. Deploying learning systems in consequential settings also requires calibrating and communicating the uncertainty of predictions. To convey instance-wise uncertainty for prediction tasks, we show how to generate set-valued predictions from a black-box predictor that control the expected loss on future test points at a user-specified level. Our approach provides explicit finite-sample guarantees for any dataset by using a holdout set to calibrate the size of the prediction sets. This framework enables simple, distribution-free, rigorous error control for many tasks, and we demonstrate it in five large-scale machine learning problems.

title: Conformal Prediction with Learned Features
abstract: We study the problem of constructing prediction intervals that attain valid coverage in finite samples while being as short as possible. Conformal prediction provides a general methodology for achieving marginal coverage, but the efficiency of the resulting intervals depends critically on the quality of the underlying score function. We propose a method for learning the score function by optimizing a differentiable approximation to the interval length, while maintaining the finite-sample coverage guarantee through a conformal calibration step. Our approach jointly trains a regression model and a score function by minimizing a soft surrogate for the prediction interval length. We prove that the resulting prediction intervals maintain finite-sample marginal coverage regardless of the quality of the learned score function, and we establish excess length bounds showing consistency under standard regularity conditions. Experiments on real and synthetic datasets show that our approach produces substantially shorter intervals than existing methods.

title: Conformal Inference of Counterfactuals and Individual Treatment Effects
abstract: Evaluating treatment effect heterogeneity widely informs treatment decision making. We propose a conformal inference approach to construct prediction intervals for counterfactuals and individual treatment effects under the potential outcomes framework. For counterfactual outcomes, we establish valid prediction intervals that cover the unobserved potential outcome with a prespecified probability. For individual treatment effects, we derive valid prediction intervals by combining two such counterfactual intervals. Our methods are fully distribution-free and model-agnostic, building on the conformal prediction framework while accommodating the unique challenges of causal inference, including the fundamental problem of missing counterfactual outcomes. We prove finite-sample validity under exchangeability and provide extensions for covariate shift and weighted conformal inference. Experiments on synthetic and semi-synthetic data demonstrate that our approach yields informative prediction intervals that maintain the desired coverage.
